key_insight: Spatial-TTT enables continuous, streaming spatial intelligence by applying lightweight test-time training to visual streams so the model adaptively selects, organizes, and retains spatial evidence rather than just extending context window size. This yields a compact, updatable spatial memory that stays consistent over long, unbounded video input.
problem_solved: How to maintain and update accurate spatial representations from ongoing, potentially unbounded video streams — selecting what to keep, how to organize it, and how to adapt online to scene changes without retraining offline.
method: Online test-time training (TTT): continuously adapt model parameters on incoming frames using self-supervised/geometric consistency objectives to stay aligned with the current scene.

Streaming spatial memory: a compact, queryable memory that selectively retains and organizes spatial evidence over time (eviction/prioritization policies) instead of naively storing long context windows.
Temporal-geometry constraints: leverage spatiotemporal and geometric consistency losses to fuse new observations into the memory while preventing drift and preserving useful long-term structure.
impact: Provides a practical way to build long-duration, robust spatial reasoning for applications like robotics, AR, and mapping by enabling models to adapt online and maintain compact, reliable spatial memories from continuous video.

paper_title: Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training
paper_authors: Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Jiawei Chi, Yimo Cai, Yi-Hsin Hung
